**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The TRANSITION rule is satisfied in substance, and the vendor-side framing of the rule does not map cleanly onto this collaboration:

- **Data return / deletion:** Section 11.6 (p0477) is a mutual, request-triggered return/destruction provision with written confirmation of destruction, and it expressly survives termination via Section 12.4 (p0532). Retention carve-outs for continuing rights/obligations and archival copies mean there is no "immediate deletion / no return" walk-away exposure for us. On expiry, our licences go perpetual, royalty-free and fully paid up (p0499).
- **Transition assistance:** Section 12.3(c)(vi) (p0516–p0525) plus 12.3(c)(iv) (p0512–p0514) provide a detailed, time-bounded transition regime (regulatory materials, pharmacovigilance data, know-how transfer, manufacturing tech transfer, clinical trial transfer, orderly-transition cooperation), and Section 12.3(e) (p0531) requires RevMed to provide copies and "all reasonable assistance" to us on a change-of-control termination.
- **Direction:** the bulk of these obligations run from Sanofi to RevMed, which is the standard licence-back bargain on termination — not something to flag against ourselves.

Noted (not flagged): the durations and effort caps in 12.3(c)(iv) and (vi) are redacted, so the practical length of our assistance obligations and the assistance available to us should be confirmed commercially rather than redlined here.
